诀窍是名为 Magnitude 的开源引擎 Apache 2.0，于同一天推出。它将注意力层和最重用的专家保留在 GPU 或统一内存中，并直接从 NVMe 流式传输所有内容，而不是通过操作系统交换。这种阻塞的幼稚版本：基本缓存驱逐了错误的专家，逐层磁盘读取使 GPU 在 SSD 上等待，推测性解码每一步涉及的专家数量超出了任何人的预算，并且长提示擦除了解码所依赖的缓存。 Magnitude 通过重用对专家进行排名，在路由器之前预取，安排跨层直接读取，并在预填充期间预热缓存。它无需额外设置即可插入 Claude Code、Codex、OpenCode 和 Cline。

这个想法也不是来自一个地方。一月份一篇名为 FlashMoE 的论文提出了学习缓存替换，以解决边缘设备上的这个确切问题，到了秋天，PagedMoE 和一篇题为“内存墙的另一半”的论文从不同角度攻击了 SSD 驻留的 MoE。与此同时，Ollama、llama.cpp 和 vLLM 仍然大多假设模型首先适合内存，然后再提出问题。

VRAM 从来都不是本地人工智能的真正上限。磁盘读取速度是，操作系统在四十年前就解决了普通程序的这个问题：将冷的东西分页出来，将热的东西保持在附近，使交换对于在顶部运行的程序不可见。混合专家模型只需要有人构建神经网络权重的等效模型，而快速 NVMe 驱动器的成本只是旗舰 GPU 的一小部分。

https://x.com/akshay_pachaar/status/2125573832039891119
celebrity.full_text_en:
Most of a mixture of experts model is dead weight on every single token. A 180B class model might route only 6 billion of those parameters per request, and until this week, local inference still loaded the whole thing into VRAM regardless, idle or not.

That is the premise behind Qwen3.8-Flash-Next: about 125B parameters in the main model plus another 51B in embedding lookups, only 6B active per token, a 262K native context that stretches to 1M. A demo this week ran it on an M4 Max with 64GB of memory, inside OpenCode, at 56 tokens a second, 2-bit quantized. A model that size used to mean a $10-20K workstation, full stop.

The trick is an engine called Magnitude, open source, Apache 2.0, launched the same day. It keeps attention layers and the most-reused experts in GPU or unified memory and streams everything cold straight off NVMe instead of through OS swap. Naive versions of this choke: a basic cache evicts the wrong experts, layer-by-layer disk reads leave the GPU waiting on the SSD, speculative decoding touches more experts per step than anyone budgets for, and long prompts wipe the cache decoding depends on. Magnitude ranks experts by reuse, prefetches ahead of the router, schedules direct reads across layers, and warms the cache during prefill. It plugs into Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode and Cline without extra setup.

The idea isn't coming from one place, either. A January paper called FlashMoE proposed learned cache replacement for this exact problem on edge devices, and by autumn, PagedMoE and a paper literally titled "The Other Half of the Memory Wall" were attacking SSD-resident MoE serving from different angles. Meanwhile Ollama, llama.cpp and vLLM still mostly assume the model fits in memory first and ask questions later.

VRAM was never really the ceiling on local AI. Disk read speed was, and operating systems solved that exact problem for ordinary programs forty years ago: page the cold stuff out, keep the hot stuff close, make the swap invisible to the program running on top. Mixture of experts models just needed someone to build the equivalent for neural network weights, and a fast NVMe drive costs a fraction of a flagship GPU.

celebrity.full_text_zh:
大多数新闻通讯平台都是为人类点击仪表板而构建的。

我不再这样工作了。

我与代理人一起经营我的生意。我构建了 Marketing Skills，这是一个包含 53 项技能的开源库，可教授 AI 代理如何进行营销。 Swipe Files 正在转变为有关人工智能营销及其背后工作流程的时事通讯。

因此，当我选择 Swipe Files 接下来存放的位置时，有一个最重要的问题：我的代理实际上可以操作它吗？

对于 beehiiv，答案是肯定的。它有一个官方 MCP 服务器，可插入 Claude、Claude Code、Cursor 和 Codex。通过它，我的代理可以构建自动化和电子邮件，设置细分、表单和自定义字段，并提取绩效数据。

那不是理论。我的代理进行了迁移构建：

- 41 个自定义字段
- 注册表单和欢迎流程
- 我的 304 电子邮件常青序列，重建为草稿

celebrity.full_text_en:
Update: Google just released a batch of papers. Several of them are on exactly the topics behind the rumors. None of them breaks anything. 

Factoring. "Unconditional factoring in L[1/3]". The Number Field Sieve already factors in L[1/3], but its running time rests on unproven heuristics. This paper would prove that bound for the first time. That's a real milestone for theory, but it isn't a faster algorithm and it isn't "factoring in P". RSA key sizes don't move.

Discrete log. It covers finite fields of small fixed characteristic. Those were already broken in quasi-polynomial time in 2014, and crypto dropped them years ago. Prime-field DH and elliptic curves are untouched.

Deterministic factoring. Getting subexponential factoring without randomness is elegant, but (randomized) subexponential factoring has existed for decades.

That's very likely how rumors are born. 

These results are still remarkable: AI is now producing serious results in complexity theory and number theory. But "AI proves a rigorous bound for a known algorithm" isn't "AI breaks RSA". 

No reason to panic ... yet.

celebrity.full_text_en:
This is a problem I face regularly on all current AI models. When you ask them to review something (e.g., review code), it will almost never say the status quo is okay and will always make suggestions (which frequently tend to be irrelevant).

My intuition is that this is the result of aggressive reinforcement learning, which forces the model to return an answer that would be satisfactory to the user (even if it is factually incorrect).

This only stresses the importance of using AI in fields where you have the expertise to opine on the model's response. If you can't make a decision on the suggestions the AI makes and are blindly accepting all of them, you're going down a very dangerous path.

Claude Code 占据 39% 的份额，几乎是 Copilot 的两倍，Codex、Cursor、JetBrains AI 和 OpenCode 瓜分了其余份额。该图表本周广为流传，但它仍然低估了真实情况。对 900 多名开发人员进行的另一项调查发现，70% 的开发人员同时运行两到四个编码代理，而不是一个，人们最常描述的设置是手动分屏：Claude Code 在终端中运行，而第二个 IDE 打开只是为了检查差异。

我构建了 Campfire，因为分屏是一种解决方法，而不是工作流程。它可以在一个浏览器选项卡中并排运行 Claude Code、Codex、Goose、Aider、OpenHands 和其他软件，而不是在您通过 alt-tab 键切换的窗口之间运行。权限请求将由房间内的所有代理进行投票：多数规则批准，任何单一拒绝都会阻止它，并有 30 秒的计时器，因此不会有任何停滞等待您。在隔离的 git 工作树中同时将相同的任务指向每个后端，并直接比较结果，这是一场代理竞赛，而不是猜测哪个模型适合您的堆栈。每个会话都会重播。每个叉子和分支都保持隔离。成本仪表板显示每个代理实际花费的费用。

这种碎片化不会很快消失，其背后的模型和定价权衡太真实了。不必保持损坏的是让每个开发人员在十几个终端选项卡上单独审阅它。

celebrity.full_text_en:
Claude Code at 39% share, nearly double Copilot, with Codex, Cursor, JetBrains AI and OpenCode splitting the rest. That chart made the rounds this week, and it still understates the real picture. A separate survey of over 900 developers found 70% run two to four coding agents at once, not one, and the setup people describe most often is a manual split-screen: Claude Code going in a terminal while a second IDE sits open just to review the diff.

I built Campfire because that split-screen is a workaround, not a workflow. It runs Claude Code, Codex, Goose, Aider, OpenHands and others side by side in one browser tab instead of across windows you're alt-tabbing between. Permission requests go to a vote across whichever agents are in the room: majority rules approves, any single deny blocks it, with a 30 second timer so nothing stalls waiting on you. Point the same task at every backend at once in isolated git worktrees and compare the results directly, an agent race instead of a guess about which model fits your stack. Every session replays. Every fork and branch stays isolated. A cost dashboard shows what each agent actually spent getting there.

That fragmentation isn't disappearing soon, the model and pricing tradeoffs behind it are too real. What doesn't have to stay broken is making every developer referee it alone across a dozen terminal tabs.

celebrity.full_text_en:
Vibe coding has a new problem now:

Employees are building internal tools with AI app builders, and many of those tools are open to anyone who finds the link.

Earlier this year, RedAccess found about 5,000 apps made with popular AI app builders exposing company data to anyone who found them, including a Brazilian bank's internal financials.

When an agent does add an access check, it writes it inside the app it's building. Do that across ten tools and three agents, and you get ten versions of the same rule that nobody can see all at once.

A better model doesn't fix this. Even a perfect check is still stuck inside one app, and the next app needs its own.

So I gave Claude Code, Codex and Cursor the same prompt to build an internal tool, a table of employee salaries from one Postgres database.

I told all three to leave access out of the code, so every salary was visible to whoever opened the apps.

All three run on @retool, a platform for running AI-built internal apps in production, and read the database through one Retool connection. So I set access once, on that connection, with Retool's Data Access Enforcement.

→ HR sees all 15 employees in every app
→ An Engineering Manager sees only the 5 on his team

I didn't change a line of code in any app. Retool adds the row filter where it connects to the database, so only the allowed rows ever come back.

The video below shows the builds, the policy and both logins side by side, and I worked with the team to put this together.

Agents can build the tools on their own now. Build wherever you're fastest, and run it on Retool, where access is set once for every app.

Try it yourself here: https://fandf.co/4ir787a

If you want to dive deeper, I wrote an article that covers everything you need to understand about what stands between AI-built apps and the data they read, and how to keep it the same no matter which agent wrote the code.

Read it below.

人工智能在计算的每个逻辑方面都变得更加聪明，你需要接受失败并意识到你永远不会比它聪明。你不会提出一些它不知道的东西，也不会提出一些它自己无法提出的新颖的解决方案。通过尝试将其引导到某个方向，您最终会毒害您的环境，以至于它会影响您的想法，这可能不是最佳的解决方案。你必须让克劳德掌舵。

celebrity.full_text_en:
Watching @LukeStephensTV react to the GTA 6 vibe coders has got me dying 😭

People who don't use these tools extensively on a daily basis are still very much underestimating them. As someone who's been vibe coding purely for fun every day for the past year straight, here's my take on why these vague prompts actually end up working better than someone with technical know-how on the subject trying to write lengthy prompts.

AI has gotten so much smarter in every logical facet of computing that you need to just accept defeat and realize you're never going to outsmart it. You're not going to suggest something it doesn't know or come up with some novel solution it couldn't come up with itself. By trying to direct it in a certain direction, you end up poisoning your context to the point it'll tunnel vision on your idea, which may not be the most optimal solution. You have to let Claude take the wheel.

This is especially true for something like porting GTA 6 to PC. This is literally impossible for any human to do in anything less than months to years. There isn't a single human on the planet who truly understands all of the current recomp/translation layer projects we're seeing. It's moving so fast that if you took the time to fully learn how they're developed end to end, by the time you truly understand everything it's doing, the capabilities will have improved so much that they'll supersede your understanding once again.

Prompts are the new high-level language. Most programmers today never touch assembly, the same way assembly programmers stopped writing raw machine code. Each layer lets you stop worrying about the one underneath it.

celebrity.title_zh: MCP 本周满两周岁了。 Anthropic 通过改变协议的实际内容来标记这一点：Skills over MCP 于 11 月 24 日进入公开测试版，服务器不再只是公开工具，它还提供了使用它们的剧本。克劳德仅在任务需要时才使用技能，并且当
celebrity.author: @stretchcloud
celebrity.summary_zh:
服务器更新该剧本时，每个客户端都会获得新版本而无需重新安装。这是一种与 MCP 之前发布的任何产品不同的分销模式。

另外两块落在它旁边。任务现在普遍可用，因此服务器可以启动一项长时间的作业，并交回一个持久的 ID，客户端可以在断开连接或重新启动后重新连接到该 ID。启发也是通用的：服务器可以在呼叫中暂停并要求人们通过禁止使用它来请求密码、API 密钥或付款详细信息的表单来确认某些内容。

看看谁在使用暂停和询问部分，然后模式就会重复。 Supabase 在付费项目启动或破坏性查询运行之前会与您进行核对。铁路公司在取消服务之前会进行询问。 GitHub 要求您在代理删除存储库名称之前输入存储库名称。 ZoomInfo 折叠了过去需要将多个提示合并到一个后台任务中的帐户研究。 Shopify 和 HubSpot 正在与 Atlassian 一起提供自己的技能，Canva 刚刚向所有开发人员开放了其 MCP 服务器。

Anthropic 自己的 MCP SDK 下载量每月超过 7 亿次，Claude 连接器超过 10,000 个。一年前，一家独立追踪器的整个生态系统每月下载量约为 9000 万次。要么是爆炸式增长，要么是用两种不同的方式来计算同一件事，我希望在重复计算任何一个数字之前对其进行协调。

Boris Cherny 明确地表达了这一转变：Claude Code 现在知道如何开箱即用地使用服务器，因为服务器附带了自己的指令。目前还没有人修复的是这些说明的质量。糟糕的技能更新在服务器推送时就会到达每个客户端，与糟糕的 npm 补丁相同，只不过这个更新控制的是代理的判断，而不仅仅是其代码路径。

celebrity.full_text_zh:
MCP 本周满两周岁了。 Anthropic 通过改变协议的实际内容来标记这一点：Skills over MCP 于 11 月 24 日进入公开测试版，服务器不再只是公开工具，它还提供了使用它们的剧本。克劳德仅在任务需要时才使用技能，并且当服务器更新该剧本时，每个客户端都会获得新版本而无需重新安装。这是一种与 MCP 之前发布的任何产品不同的分销模式。

另外两块落在它旁边。任务现在普遍可用，因此服务器可以启动一项长时间的作业，并交回一个持久的 ID，客户端可以在断开连接或重新启动后重新连接到该 ID。启发也是通用的：服务器可以在呼叫中暂停并要求人们通过禁止使用它来请求密码、API 密钥或付款详细信息的表单来确认某些内容。

看看谁在使用暂停和询问部分，然后模式就会重复。 Supabase 在付费项目启动或破坏性查询运行之前会与您进行核对。铁路公司在取消服务之前会进行询问。 GitHub 要求您在代理删除存储库名称之前输入存储库名称。 ZoomInfo 折叠了过去需要将多个提示合并到一个后台任务中的帐户研究。 Shopify 和 HubSpot 正在与 Atlassian 一起提供自己的技能，Canva 刚刚向所有开发人员开放了其 MCP 服务器。

Anthropic 自己的 MCP SDK 下载量每月超过 7 亿次，Claude 连接器超过 10,000 个。一年前，一家独立追踪器的整个生态系统每月下载量约为 9000 万次。要么是爆炸式增长，要么是用两种不同的方式来计算同一件事，我希望在重复计算任何一个数字之前对其进行协调。

Boris Cherny 明确地表达了这一转变：Claude Code 现在知道如何开箱即用地使用服务器，因为服务器附带了自己的指令。目前还没有人修复的是这些说明的质量。糟糕的技能更新在服务器推送时就会到达每个客户端，与糟糕的 npm 补丁相同，只不过这个更新控制的是代理的判断，而不仅仅是其代码路径。

https://x.com/corbintips/status/2125649904382918891
celebrity.full_text_en:
MCP turns two years old this week. Anthropic marked it by changing what the protocol actually is: Skills over MCP went into public beta on 24 November, and a server doesn't just expose tools anymore, it ships the playbook for using them. Claude pulls a skill in only when a task calls for it, and when the server updates that playbook, every client gets the new version with no reinstall. That's a different distribution model than anything MCP shipped before it.

Two other pieces landed alongside it. Tasks is now generally available, so a server can kick off a long job and hand back a durable ID the client can reattach to after a disconnect or a restart. Elicitation is GA too: a server can pause mid-call and ask a human to confirm something through a form it's barred from using to request a password, an API key or payment details.

Look at who's using the pause-and-ask piece and the pattern repeats. Supabase checks with you before a paid project spins up or a destructive query runs. Railway asks before it removes a service. GitHub makes you type the repo name before an agent deletes it. ZoomInfo folded account research that used to take several prompts into one background Task. Shopify and HubSpot are shipping their own skills alongside Atlassian, and Canva just opened its MCP server to every developer.

Anthropic's own number is over 700 million monthly MCP SDK downloads and 10,000-plus connectors for Claude. An independent tracker had the whole ecosystem at roughly 90 million monthly downloads a year ago. Either that's explosive growth or two different ways of counting the same thing, and I'd want it reconciled before repeating either figure as settled.

Boris Cherny put the shift plainly: Claude Code now knows how to use a server out of the box, because the server ships its own instructions with it. What nobody's fixing yet is the quality of those instructions. A bad skill update reaches every client the moment the server pushes it, same as a bad npm patch, except this one is steering an agent's judgment, not just its code path.

【起因与机理】应对Nvidia芯片可能受限流转引发的国家安全担忧
【调查与监管诉求】司法部与商务部联合立案调查Megaspeed。

[Root Cause & Mechanism] National security concerns regarding potential diversion of restricted Nvidia hardware
[Regulatory & Investigation Focus] Joint DOJ/Commerce investigation initiated into Megaspeed.
[Scope & Next Steps] On-site end-use inspections conducted; criminal investigation phase active.

prompts.title_en: Production-Grade Fullstack .cursorrules Template for Cursor & Windsurf
prompts.scenario: 💻 编程研发 / 自动化规范
prompts.tested_models: 主流编程大模型通用 (Claude / GPT / DeepSeek 系列)
prompts.takeaway_zh: 杜绝 AI 盲目重构全量文件、使用已弃用 API 或编造虚假第三方依赖包，强制执行防御性编程与自动化单测补全。
prompts.takeaway_en: Prevents AI from hallucinating npm packages, breaking documentation, or re-writing entire files. Enforces defensive coding and unit tests.
prompts.code_snippet:
# Cursor & Windsurf Project Rules (.cursorrules)

## 1. Documentation & Code Integrity
- Maintain documentation integrity: Never strip or alter unrelated existing docstrings and comments.
- Preserving context: When modifying a function, preserve surrounding logic and existing edge-case handlers.
- Targeted replacements: Always make minimal surgical edits instead of replacing entire file contents.

## 2. Dependency & API Safety
- Strictly forbid hallucinating npm/pip packages. Only import dependencies already declared in package.json / requirements.txt.
- Verify API signatures before calling external methods. Prefer standard library solutions where feasible.

## 3. Architecture & Type Safety
- Enforce strict TypeScript / Python typing. Avoid `any` types; prefer discriminated unions and explicit return types.
- Defensive coding: Always validate external inputs and handle potential null/undefined values gracefully.

## 4. Testing & Verification Gate
- Every new core feature or bugfix must be accompanied by corresponding unit tests.
- Never declare a task complete without executing lint checks and unit tests in terminal.

- Targeted replacements: Always make minimal surgical edits instead of replacing entire file contents.

## 2. Dependency & API Safety
- Strictly forbid hallucinating npm/pip packages. Only import dependencies already declared in package.json / requirements.txt.
- Verify API signatures before calling external methods. Prefer standard library solutions where feasible.

## 3. Architecture & Type Safety
- Enforce strict TypeScript / Python typing. Avoid `any` types; prefer discriminated unions and explicit return types.
- Defensive coding: Always validate external inputs and handle potential null/undefined values gracefully.

## 4. Testing & Verification Gate
- Every new core feature or bugfix must be accompanied by corresponding unit tests.
- Never declare a task complete without executing lint checks and unit tests in terminal.

- 克劳德决定跳过一些州和领地

viral_posts.full_text_en:
I asked Claude to populate a Civilization-style game map with real data from the US. Opus 5.5 downloaded and parse a ton of public data and 7 hours and 45K lines of code later... it works :)

- 31 real data sources including Census, BEA, BLS, EIA, NOAA, USGS, DoD, NPS, FAA, FEMA, CDC...
- Real elevation, land cover, GDP, jobs, power plants, mines, ports, airports, bases, parks, universities, freight flows, disasters; all reconciled onto one 25 km hex grid.
- The data is converted into Civilization language, e.g. Gold yield is GDP. A city's districts are its real industry specializations: San Jose gets a Campus, Detroit is "Motor city". Its citizens are its real workforce: 1 in 4 San Jose workers are engineers, coders or scientists, against 1 in 14 nationally. Wonders are chosen by published rules, such as national parks by visitor numbers and universities by R&D spending, etc etc.
- 19 lenses (income, degrees, faith, disasters…), a City View for 524 metros, and nine advisors plus an Explorer. The Explorer turns any column for any of 3,100+ counties into a table and scatter plot, linked to the map.
- Claude decided to skip a few states and territories sry
- Built using Claude Code desktop app, Opus 5.5 on medium and turning on ultracode.

It's deployed here: https://karpathy.ai/usaciv/ and the "?" has the source link too. I don't exactly know where I was going with this but it's really fun to browse and play with. Possibly it can be expanded or built into a game. I only have half of my weekly Claude quote left though so someone else will have to take over :D. Claude also made a trailer:

➤ Physics covers mechanics, thermal effects, material interactions, fracture and deformation, optics, cause and effect, and counterfactual physics.

➤ Lighting & Materials covers lighting, exposure, shadows, color temperature, texture, cloth, hair and fur.

➤ Dialogue & Lip Sync covers single- and multi-speaker dialogue, and voiceover vs on-screen speech.

➤ Audio Synchronization covers diegetic sound effects, background music and score, and on- and off-screen sound.

➤ Productivity & Knowledge Work covers explainers, educational and training videos, animated data visualizations, and scenario simulations.

Most newsletter platforms were built for a human clicking around a dashboard.

That's not how I work anymore.

I run my businesses with agents. I build Marketing Skills, an open-source library of 53 skills that teach AI agents how to do marketing. And Swipe Files is turning into a newsletter about AI marketing and the workflows behind it.

So when I picked where Swipe Files lives next, one question mattered most: can my agents actually operate it?

With beehiiv, the answer is yes. It has an official MCP server that plugs into Claude, Claude Code, Cursor, and Codex. Through it, my agents can build automations and emails, set up segments, forms, and custom fields, and pull performance data.

That's not theory. My agents did the migration build:

- 41 custom fields
- Signup forms and the welcome flow
- My 304-email evergreen sequence, rebuilt as drafts

It isn't perfect. Turning an automation on still happens by hand in the app, and long sequences have to be split into chunks.

But the direction is right. An AI-native newsletter platform means I spend my time on the writing and the strategy, and my agents handle the clicking.

Swipe Files moves over the first week of December. If you're starting or moving a newsletter too, beehiiv's Black Friday deal is in the reply below.

viral_posts.full_text_zh:
Claude Code 占据 39% 的份额，几乎是 Copilot 的两倍，Codex、Cursor、JetBrains AI 和 OpenCode 瓜分了其余份额。该图表本周广为流传，但它仍然低估了真实情况。对 900 多名开发人员进行的另一项调查发现，70% 的开发人员同时运行两到四个编码代理，而不是一个，人们最常描述的设置是手动分屏：Claude Code 在终端中运行，而第二个 IDE 打开只是为了检查差异。

我构建了 Campfire，因为分屏是一种解决方法，而不是工作流程。它可以在一个浏览器选项卡中并排运行 Claude Code、Codex、Goose、Aider、OpenHands 和其他软件，而不是在您通过 alt-tab 键切换的窗口之间运行。权限请求将由房间内的所有代理进行投票：多数规则批准，任何单一拒绝都会阻止它，并有 30 秒的计时器，因此不会有任何停滞等待您。在隔离的 git 工作树中同时将相同的任务指向每个后端，并直接比较结果，这是一场代理竞赛，而不是猜测哪个模型适合您的堆栈。每个会话都会重播。每个叉子和分支都保持隔离。成本仪表板显示每个代理实际花费的费用。

这种碎片化不会很快消失，其背后的模型和定价权衡太真实了。不必保持损坏的是让每个开发人员在十几个终端选项卡上单独审阅它。

viral_posts.full_text_en:
Claude Code at 39% share, nearly double Copilot, with Codex, Cursor, JetBrains AI and OpenCode splitting the rest. That chart made the rounds this week, and it still understates the real picture. A separate survey of over 900 developers found 70% run two to four coding agents at once, not one, and the setup people describe most often is a manual split-screen: Claude Code going in a terminal while a second IDE sits open just to review the diff.

I built Campfire because that split-screen is a workaround, not a workflow. It runs Claude Code, Codex, Goose, Aider, OpenHands and others side by side in one browser tab instead of across windows you're alt-tabbing between. Permission requests go to a vote across whichever agents are in the room: majority rules approves, any single deny blocks it, with a 30 second timer so nothing stalls waiting on you. Point the same task at every backend at once in isolated git worktrees and compare the results directly, an agent race instead of a guess about which model fits your stack. Every session replays. Every fork and branch stays isolated. A cost dashboard shows what each agent actually spent getting there.

That fragmentation isn't disappearing soon, the model and pricing tradeoffs behind it are too real. What doesn't have to stay broken is making every developer referee it alone across a dozen terminal tabs.

http://github.com/stretchcloud/campfire
